questions.question: How many forms does the future tense take?
questions.explanation: In future time, the verb takes four forms: the simple future, future continuous, future perfect and future perfect continuous.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a form of the future tense?
questions.explanation: The four future tense forms are simple future, future continuous, future perfect and future perfect continuous. 'Future past' is not a form.

questions.question: The future tense is used to talk about actions that will take place:
questions.explanation: The future tense is used to talk about actions that will take place in the future.

questions.question: What is the form of the simple future tense?
options: Will/shall + base form of the verb
questions.explanation: The simple future tense takes the form will/shall + base form of the verb.

questions.question: What is the form of the future continuous tense?
options: Will/shall + base form of the verb
Will be + base form of the verb + -ing
questions.explanation: The future continuous tense takes the form will be + base form of the verb + -ing.

questions.question: What is the form of the future perfect tense?
options: Will have + past participle form of the verb
Will/shall + base form of the verb
questions.explanation: The future perfect tense takes the form will have + past participle form of the verb.

questions.question: What is the form of the future perfect continuous tense?
options: Will/shall + base form of the verb
Will have been + participle form of the verb
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous tense takes the form will have been + participle form of the verb.

questions.question: Will and shall are used to talk about something we have:
questions.explanation: Will and shall are used to talk about something we have just decided to do.

questions.question: In 'I will help you organize your birthday party,' 'will' expresses:
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used to express willingness to do something.

questions.question: In 'I will finish my homework today,' 'will' expresses:
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used to express an intention.

questions.question: In 'I hope we will go for a long holiday,' 'will' is used to talk about:
options: Something we hope or expect will happen
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used to talk about something we hope or expect will happen.

questions.question: What does 'going to' refer to?
options: Actions that happened in the past
Actions that will happen in the future
questions.explanation: Going to is often used to refer to actions that will happen in the future.

questions.question: In 'I am going to call you,' 'going to' indicates:
options: An indefinite time in the future
A definite intention in the near future
questions.explanation: 'I am going to call you' indicates a definite intention in the near future.

questions.question: In 'We are going to spend the holidays at my grandmother's house,' 'going to' is used for:
options: Something that happened in the past
questions.explanation: We use 'going to' to talk about something we have already planned or decided to do.

questions.question: In 'The clouds are very dark. It is going to rain,' 'going to' is used for:
options: Something we expect to happen in the immediate future
questions.explanation: 'Going to' is used to talk about something we expect to happen in the immediate future.

questions.question: Underline the correct option: Are you going to/Will you answer the phone for me, please? I'm working.
questions.explanation: 'Will you' is used for a polite request.

questions.question: Underline the correct option: I hope Sachin will/is going to visit us soon.
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used to talk about something we hope will happen.

questions.question: Underline the correct option: As decided, we will/are going to watch a film tonight.
questions.explanation: 'Are going to' is used for something already planned or decided.

questions.question: Underline the correct option: Watch out! That vase will/is going to fall on you!
questions.explanation: 'Is going to' is used for something we expect to happen in the immediate future.

questions.question: Underline the correct option: Please take an umbrella. It looks like it will/is going to rain.
questions.explanation: 'Is going to' is used for something we expect to happen in the immediate future.

questions.question: The simple future tense is used for actions that:
options: Will happen at some point of time in the future
questions.explanation: The simple future tense is used for actions that will happen at some point of time in the future.

questions.question: In 'Bipin will play as the main striker in the football match,' the simple future is used for:
options: An action that will happen in the future
questions.explanation: The simple future 'will play' describes an action that will happen in the future.

questions.question: In 'It will rain tomorrow,' 'will' is used to:
options: Predict an event in the near future
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used to predict an event in the immediate or near future.

questions.question: In 'We will buy the house,' 'will' is used to:
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used to express a decision or willingness to do something.

questions.question: In 'Shall I get some coffee for you?' 'shall' is used to:
questions.explanation: 'Shall' is used to make an offer or a suggestion.

questions.question: In 'What shall I make for dinner?' 'shall' is used to:
questions.explanation: 'Shall' is used to ask for advice or instructions.

questions.question: The simple present tense can be used to describe:
options: Future actions or events, especially those that are part of a schedule
questions.explanation: The simple present tense can be used to describe future actions or events, especially actions that take place in the future as part of a schedule.

questions.question: In 'The film starts at 8 p.m. tonight,' the simple present 'starts' refers to:
questions.explanation: The simple present is used for future events that are part of a schedule. 'The film starts at 8 p.m. tonight' refers to a future action.

questions.question: In 'Our school re-opens after vacations next week,' the simple present 're-opens' refers to:
questions.explanation: The simple present is used for future events that are part of a schedule. 'Re-opens' refers to a future action.

questions.question: The present continuous may be used to refer to future events or actions, especially when they are:
questions.explanation: The present continuous may be used to refer to future events or actions, especially when they are part of a definite plan.

questions.question: In 'We are having a birthday party on Saturday,' the present continuous 'are having' refers to:
questions.explanation: The present continuous is used for a future event that is part of a definite plan.

questions.question: In 'I am meeting my cousins today,' the present continuous 'am meeting' refers to:
questions.explanation: The present continuous is used for a future event that is part of a definite plan.

questions.question: In 'Tara is having lunch with me in the afternoon,' the present continuous 'is having' refers to:
questions.explanation: The present continuous is used for a future event that is part of a definite plan.

questions.question: In 'We are visiting our cousins next week,' the present continuous 'are visiting' refers to:
questions.explanation: The present continuous is used for a future event that is part of a definite plan.

questions.question: In 'The mall closes at 6 p.m. today,' the simple present 'closes' refers to:
questions.explanation: The simple present is used for future events that are part of a schedule.

questions.question: In 'We are having dinner,' the present continuous 'are having' refers to:
questions.explanation: 'We are having dinner' describes an action happening at the moment of speaking.

questions.question: In 'I begin my music classes soon,' the simple present 'begin' refers to:
questions.explanation: The simple present is used for future events that are part of a schedule.

questions.question: In 'I visit my friends on weekends,' the simple present 'visit' refers to:
questions.explanation: 'I visit my friends on weekends' describes a habitual action.

questions.question: The future continuous tense is used for actions that:
options: Will start in the future and continue for some time
questions.explanation: The future continuous tense is used for actions that will start in the future and continue for some time.

questions.question: In 'Prerita will be starting dance classes from next week,' the future continuous is used for:
options: An action that will start in the future and continue
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be starting' describes an action that will start in the future and continue for some time.

questions.question: Fill in: I have severe toothache. I ______ the dentist. (visit)
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be visiting' is used for an action that will start in the future and continue.

questions.question: Fill in: Dina ______ for the birthday party. (come)
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be coming' is used for an action that will start in the future and continue.

questions.question: Fill in: We ______ our holidays in Delhi this year. (spend)
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be spending' is used for an action that will start in the future and continue.

questions.question: Fill in: We ______ lots of mangoes from Mumbai. (get)
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be getting' is used for an action that will start in the future and continue.

questions.question: Fill in: By this time next week, I ______ in Singapore. (work)
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be working' is used for an action that will be in progress at a specific time in the future.

questions.question: Fill in: ______ you ______ the concert this year? (attend)
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be attending' is used for an action that will be in progress.

questions.question: Fill in: The Ghosh family ______ to Kerala this summer. (fly)
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be flying' is used for an action that will start in the future and continue.

questions.question: Fill in: ______ Tandra ______ with you in April? (stay)
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be staying' is used for an action that will be in progress.

questions.question: The future perfect tense is used to talk about a future activity that:
options: Will be finished by or before a specific time in the future
questions.explanation: The future perfect tense is used to talk about a future activity that will be finished by or before a specific time in the future.

questions.question: In 'By 4 o'clock tomorrow, the train will have left,' the future perfect is used for:
options: An action that will be finished before a specific future time
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have left' describes an action that will be finished by a specific time in the future.

questions.question: Fill in: Tarun and Aditi ______ by this time tomorrow. (arrive)
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have arrived' is used for an action that will be finished by a specific time in the future.

questions.question: Fill in: I ______ my homework by tomorrow. (complete)
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have completed' is used for an action that will be finished by a specific time in the future.

questions.question: Fill in: Daniel ______ a complaint against his landlord by this evening. (lodge)
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have lodged' is used for an action that will be finished by a specific time in the future.

questions.question: Fill in: Sunita's mother ______ her lunch before she leaves for work. (pack)
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have packed' is used for an action that will be finished before another future action.

questions.question: Fill in: The old man ______ the puppy by noon. (feed)
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have fed' is used for an action that will be finished by a specific time in the future.

questions.question: Fill in: The parrot ______ a new song by this time next week. (learn)
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have learned' is used for an action that will be finished by a specific time in the future.

questions.question: The future perfect continuous tense is used to talk about an ongoing activity which:
options: Has not yet been completed but will be at a specified time in the future
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous tense is used to talk about an ongoing activity which has not yet been completed but will be at a specified time in the future.

questions.question: In 'Next month, Kiran will have been taking singing lessons for ten years,' the future perfect continuous is used for:
options: An ongoing activity that will continue up to a specified future time
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been taking' describes an ongoing activity that will continue up to a specified time in the future.

questions.question: Fill in: By next June, we ______ on the project for three months. (work)
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been working' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Fill in: I ______ the house for two hours when it strikes ten. (clean)
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been cleaning' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Fill in: The class ______ on over one hour by the time the bell rings. (go)
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been going' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Fill in: Come August, we ______ in Mumbai for five years. (live)
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been living' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Fill in: By the time I attend the next school reunion, I ______ for nearly five years. (work)
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been working' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Fill in: By 2017, Sarojini ______ as a professional singer for a decade. (perform)
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been performing' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Fill in: They ______ abroad for two years by this time next year. (stay)
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been staying' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Fill in: By today, it ______ for three days continuously. (rain)
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been raining' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the simple future?
options: She will return after one hour.
She will be returning after one hour.
She will have returned after one hour.
She will have been returning after one hour.
questions.explanation: The simple future 'will return' is used for an action that will happen at some point in the future.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the future continuous?
options: She will be meeting the children on Friday.
She will meet the children on Friday.
She will have met the children on Friday.
She will have been meeting the children on Friday.
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be meeting' is used for an action that will be in progress.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the future perfect?
options: My elder brother will complete his tenth grade by 2020.
My elder brother will be completing his tenth grade by 2020.
My elder brother will have completed his tenth grade by 2020.
My elder brother will have been completing his tenth grade by 2020.
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have completed' is used for an action that will be finished by a specific time in the future.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the future perfect continuous?
options: They will work on this project for six months by the end of next week.
They will be working on this project for six months by the end of next week.
They will have worked on this project for six months by the end of next week.
They will have been working on this project for six months by the end of next week.
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been working' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'going to' for something already planned or decided?
options: I am going to help my mother in the kitchen today.
I will help you organize your birthday party.
I shall get some coffee for you.
What shall I make for dinner?
questions.explanation: 'Going to' is used for something already planned or decided. 'I am going to help my mother' expresses a prior decision.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'going to' for something expected to happen in the immediate future?
options: We are going to spend the holidays at my grandmother's house.
I will finish my homework today.
Watch out! That tree is going to fall!
I hope we will go for a long holiday.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' is used to talk about something we expect to happen in the immediate future.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the simple present for a future scheduled event?
options: The film starts at 8 p.m. tonight.
The film is starting at 8 p.m. tonight.
The film will start at 8 p.m. tonight.
The film will be starting at 8 p.m. tonight.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'starts' is used for future events that are part of a schedule.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the present continuous for a future event that is part of a definite plan?
options: We will have a birthday party on Saturday.
We will be having a birthday party on Saturday.
We have a birthday party on Saturday.
We are having a birthday party on Saturday.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'are having' is used for a future event that is part of a definite plan.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the future perfect continuous?
options: By this time next year, Mridul will play professional football for two years.
By this time next year, Mridul will be playing professional football for two years.
By this time next year, Mridul will have played professional football for two years.
By this time next year, Mridul will have been playing professional football for two years.
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been playing' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the future perfect?
options: By the time you get home, I will make dinner.
By the time you get home, I will be making dinner.
By the time you get home, I will have made dinner.
By the time you get home, I will have been making dinner.
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have made' is used for an action that will be finished before another future action.

questions.question: Complete the letter: How ______ (you be, present perfect)?
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'have you been' is used to ask about someone's state.

questions.question: Complete the letter: ______ (you come, simple future) home next month?
questions.explanation: The simple future 'will you come' is used to ask about a future action.

questions.question: Complete the letter: I ______ (write, present continuous) to you for some advice.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'am writing' is used for an action happening now.

questions.question: Complete the letter: I ______ (think, present continuous) of taking up a summer job as an intern with an NGO.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'am thinking' is used for an action happening now.

questions.question: Complete the letter: I ______ (apply, future continuous) to HelpAge India.
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be applying' is used for an action that will be in progress.

questions.question: Complete the letter: ______ (you know, simple present) of any others that I ______ (can, simple present) apply to?
questions.explanation: The simple present 'do you know' and 'can' are used in this context.

questions.question: Complete the letter: I ______ (also look, simple future) at other options for summer employment.
questions.explanation: The simple future 'will also look' is used for a future action.

questions.question: Complete the letter: By this time next year, I ______ (volunteer, future perfect continuous) at NGOs for two years.
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been volunteering' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Complete the letter: I ______ (gain, future perfect) useful experience.
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have gained' is used for an action that will be finished by a specific future time.

questions.question: Complete the letter: But I ______ (want, simple present) to do more.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'want' is used for a present state.

questions.question: Complete the letter: Since you ______ (do, present perfect) such work before, please ______ (send, simple present) me some suggestions.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'have done' is used for a past action with present relevance, and the simple present 'send' is used for a request.

questions.question: Fill in using the simple future: Tomorrow's English class ______ for about 30 minutes. (continue)
questions.explanation: The simple future 'will continue' is used for an action that will happen in the future.

questions.question: Fill in using the future continuous: Meet me at the park tomorrow. I ______ close to the main gate. (sit)
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be sitting' is used for an action that will be in progress.

questions.question: Fill in: The trophy ______ to the best team. (go)
questions.explanation: The simple future 'will go' is used for an action that will happen in the future.

questions.question: Fill in: By this time next year, my sister ______ going to her new school. (start)
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have started' is used for an action that will be finished by a specific future time.

questions.question: Fill in: Sia ______ for Reema at her house for over two hours now. (wait)
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous 'will have been waiting' is used for an ongoing activity up to a specified future time.

questions.question: Fill in using the simple future: I ______ my grandmother next summer. (visit)
questions.explanation: The simple future 'will visit' is used for an action that will happen in the future.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the simple present for a future scheduled event?
options: The mall is closing at 6 p.m. today.
The mall will close at 6 p.m. today.
The mall closes at 6 p.m. today.
The mall will be closing at 6 p.m. today.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'closes' is used for future events that are part of a schedule.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the present continuous for a future event?
options: He will leave for Chandigarh at 8 o'clock tonight.
He leaves for Chandigarh at 8 o'clock tonight.
He is leaving for Chandigarh at 8 o'clock tonight.
He will be leaving for Chandigarh at 8 o'clock tonight.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'is leaving' is used for a future event that is part of a definite plan.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'will' to express an intention?
options: I will finish my homework today.
I am going to finish my homework today.
I will have finished my homework today.
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used to express an intention. 'I will finish my homework today' expresses an intention.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'shall' to make a suggestion?
options: Shall I get some coffee for you?
What shall I make for dinner?
Shall we go to the park?
questions.explanation: 'Shall' is used to make a suggestion. 'Shall we go to the park?' is a suggestion.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'shall' to ask for advice?
options: Shall I get some coffee for you?
Shall we go to the park?
What shall I make for dinner?
questions.explanation: 'Shall' is used to ask for advice or instructions. 'What shall I make for dinner?' asks for advice.

questions.question: Fill in: If you want, I ______ bring a cake for the get-together.
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used to express willingness to do something.

questions.question: They have already decided. Shyam and Ritesh ______ collect all the newspapers and recycle them.
questions.explanation: 'Are going to' is used for something already planned or decided.
